lines.text: Nine o'clock. Before any real work, you type the same three prompts into three agents.
You're the scheduler, and the messenger. Agent R Q does both: schedules, events, webhooks and workflows.
Ada gives storefront a task. Read last night's error log, and open a task for every new error.
Then she puts it on a schedule: daily, at nine. The footer shows the cron line and the next run.
Every run is a normal task, with its own thread. And runs never pile up.
Now the messenger job. Ada creates an event: A P I changed.
Docs and mobile subscribe to it. When it fires, each gets a task that says exactly what changed.
Billing's agent finishes, publishes the event, and both tasks start at once.
Even GitHub can start the work. A webhook turns a failed build on main into C I failed.
So when the build breaks at three, storefront's agent gets the failure. Before anyone wakes up.
And a workflow chains it all. Billing deploys first. Then docs and mobile follow, side by side.
Each step lands as a task in its own workspace. Put the first one on a schedule, and the release runs every Friday.
Schedules, events, webhooks and workflows. What would you automate first? Tell us in the comments, and try it at Agent R Q dot com.
